title: Game of Life: One Generation
description:
Conway's Game of Life is played on a grid of cells, each alive (1) or dead (0). Every cell has up to 8 neighbours (horizontal, vertical, diagonal). Cells outside the grid are always dead. All cells update simultaneously:

  • A live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbours stays alive; otherwise it dies.
  • A dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbours becomes alive.

Print the grid after one generation.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 50.

Input

The first line contains two integers R C. The next R lines each contain C space-separated values, each 0 or 1.

Output

Print the next generation as R lines of C space-separated values.

title: Search in a Sorted 2D Matrix
description:
Every row of the matrix is sorted in non-decreasing order from left to right, and every column is sorted in non-decreasing order from top to bottom. Answer Q queries: is the value x present in the matrix?

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 40, 1 ≤ Q ≤ 500, values fit in 32-bit integers. An O(R + C) per query search (start at the top-right corner) is expected.

Input

The first line contains R C, followed by R lines of C integers. Then a line with Q, followed by Q lines each containing one integer x.

Output

For each query print Yes if x occurs in the matrix, otherwise No, one per line.

title: Diagonal Zigzag Traversal
description:
Traverse the matrix along its anti-diagonals (cells with equal i + j), starting from the top-left cell. Diagonals alternate direction: the 1st diagonal (i + j = 0) goes up-right, the 2nd goes down-left, the 3rd up-right, and so on. Going up-right means from larger row index to smaller; down-left means from smaller row index to larger.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 50.

Input

The first line contains two integers R C. The next R lines each contain C space-separated integers.

Output

Print all elements in traversal order on a single line, separated by spaces.

Example: [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]] gives 1 2 4 7 5 3 6 8 9.
solution:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
a = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(r)]
res = []
for d in range(r + c - 1):
    cells = [(i, d - i) for i in range(max(0, d - c + 1), min(r - 1, d) + 1)]
    if d % 2 == 0:
        cells.reverse()
    res.extend(a[i][j] for i, j in cells)
print(" ".join(map(str, res)))

title: Spiral Fill of a Rectangle
description:
Create an N x M grid and fill it with the numbers 1, 2, ..., N·M in clockwise spiral order, starting at the top-left cell and moving right first.

Constraints: 1 ≤ N, M ≤ 30.

Input

One line with two integers N M (rows and columns).

Output

Print N lines, each with M numbers separated by single spaces (no padding).
solution:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [[0] * m for _ in range(n)]
dr, dc = [0, 1, 0, -1], [1, 0, -1, 0]
i = j = d = 0
for v in range(1, n * m + 1):
    g[i][j] = v
    ni, nj = i + dr[d], j + dc[d]
    if not (0 <= ni < n and 0 <= nj < m and g[ni][nj] == 0):
        d = (d + 1) % 4
        ni, nj = i + dr[d], j + dc[d]
    i, j = ni, nj
for row in g:
    print(" ".join(map(str, row)))

title: Toeplitz Matrix Check
description:
A matrix is Toeplitz if every diagonal running from top-left to bottom-right contains identical elements, i.e. a[i][j] = a[i-1][j-1] whenever both cells exist.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 50.

Input

The first line contains two integers R C. The next R lines each contain C space-separated integers.

Output

Print Toeplitz or Not Toeplitz.
solution:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
a = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(r)]
ok = all(a[i][j] == a[i - 1][j - 1] for i in range(1, r) for j in range(1, c))
print("Toeplitz" if ok else "Not Toeplitz")

title: Island Perimeter
description:
The grid contains land (1) and water (0). Each land cell is a unit square. Compute the total perimeter of all land: count every edge of a land cell that touches water or the outside of the grid. There may be several islands (add up all of them) or none at all.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 50.

Input

The first line contains two integers R C. The next R lines each contain C space-separated values, each 0 or 1.

Output

Print a single integer: the total perimeter.

title: Minesweeper Counts
description:
A Minesweeper board has mines (*) and empty cells (.). Replace every empty cell with the number of mines among its up to 8 neighbouring cells (horizontal, vertical and diagonal). Mines stay as *. Empty cells with no adjacent mines become 0.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 60.

Input

The first line contains R C. The next R lines each contain a string of exactly C characters, each * or ..

Output

Print the resulting board as R strings of length C (no spaces).

title: Magic Square Check
description:
A square matrix is a magic square if the sums of every row, every column, and both main diagonals are all equal. (The numbers do not have to be distinct.) Check whether the given N x N matrix is a magic square.

Constraints: 1 ≤ N ≤ 30, values may be negative.

Input

The first line contains N. The next N lines each contain N space-separated integers.

Output

If it is a magic square, print Magic followed by a space and the common sum. Otherwise print Not Magic.
solution:
n = int(input())
a = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]
sums = [sum(row) for row in a]
sums += [sum(a[i][j] for i in range(n)) for j in range(n)]
sums.append(sum(a[i][i] for i in range(n)))
sums.append(sum(a[i][n - 1 - i] for i in range(n)))
print("Magic " + str(sums[0]) if len(set(sums)) == 1 else "Not Magic")

title: Largest Square of 1s
description:
Given a binary grid, find the largest square sub-grid consisting entirely of 1s and print its area. If the grid has no 1, the answer is 0.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 120. An O(R·C) dynamic programming solution is expected.

Input

The first line contains R C. The next R lines each contain a string of exactly C characters, each 0 or 1 (no spaces).

Output

Print a single integer: the area of the largest all-ones square.

title: Integer Determinant
description:
Compute the determinant of an N x N integer matrix. The answer is always an integer; compute it exactly (no floating-point rounding errors).

Constraints: 1 ≤ N ≤ 6, |a[i][j]| ≤ 100.

Input

The first line contains N. The next N lines each contain N space-separated integers.

Output

Print the determinant as an integer.

title: 2D Range Sum Queries
description:
Given an R x C matrix, answer Q queries. Each query gives a rectangle by its top-left corner (r1, c1) and bottom-right corner (r2, c2) (1-based, inclusive). Print the sum of all elements inside the rectangle.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 50, 1 ≤ Q ≤ 1000, |a[i][j]| ≤ 1000. Precompute 2D prefix sums so each query is answered in O(1).

Input

The first line contains R C, followed by R lines of C integers. Then a line with Q, followed by Q lines each containing r1 c1 r2 c2 (r1 ≤ r2, c1 ≤ c2).

Output

Print the answer to each query on its own line.
solution:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
a = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(r)]
ps = [[0] * (c + 1) for _ in range(r + 1)]
for i in range(r):
    for j in range(c):
        ps[i + 1][j + 1] = a[i][j] + ps[i][j + 1] + ps[i + 1][j] - ps[i][j]
q = int(input())
out = []
for _ in range(q):
    r1, c1, r2, c2 = map(int, input().split())
    out.append(ps[r2][c2] - ps[r1 - 1][c2] - ps[r2][c1 - 1] + ps[r1 - 1][c1 - 1])
print("\n".join(map(str, out)))

title: Tic-Tac-Toe Verdict
description:
You are given a 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe board where X always moves first and players alternate. A player wins by having three marks in a row, column, or diagonal; the game stops as soon as someone wins. Determine the state of the board:

  • Invalid — the board cannot occur in a real game: the number of X's is not equal to the number of O's or one more; or both players have a winning line; or X has a line but the counts are equal; or O has a line but X has more marks than O.
  • X wins / O wins — a valid board where that player has a winning line (X may have two lines through the final move).
  • Draw — valid, no winner, and the board is full.
  • Ongoing — valid, no winner, and empty cells remain.

Input

Three lines, each a string of 3 characters from X, O, . (empty).

Output

Print exactly one of: Invalid, X wins, O wins, Draw, Ongoing.

title: Robot Walk with Obstacles
description:
A robot is on a grid of free cells (.), walls (#), and its start cell (S, which is free). It starts facing North (up). It executes a string of commands:

  • L — turn 90° left; R — turn 90° right.
  • F — move one cell forward. If that cell is a wall or outside the grid, the robot does not move (the command is wasted).

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 50, command string length up to 5000.

Input

The first line contains R C, then R lines of C characters forming the grid (exactly one S). The last line contains the command string (non-empty).

Output

Line 1: the final position and direction as row col D (1-based, D is one of N E S W).
Line 2: the number of distinct cells the robot occupied during the walk, including the start.
Line 3: the number of wasted F commands.

title: Bank Teller Queue Simulation
description:
A bank has K tellers numbered 1..K, all free at time 0. N customers arrive; customer i arrives at time ti and needs di minutes of service. Customers are served strictly in input order (first come, first served; arrival times are non-decreasing).

When it is customer i's turn, they start at time start = max(ti, earliest time any teller is free) and go to the lowest-numbered teller that is free at time start. They finish at start + di, and their waiting time is start - ti.

Constraints: 1 ≤ N ≤ 2000, 1 ≤ K ≤ 20, 0 ≤ ti ≤ 106, 1 ≤ di ≤ 1000.

Input

The first line contains N K. The next N lines each contain ti di.

Output

For each customer in order print teller finish_time on its own line. On the final line print the average waiting time rounded to 2 decimal places, as produced by Python's f"{x:.2f}".
solution:
n, k = map(int, input().split())
free = [0] * k
total_wait = 0
out = []
for _ in range(n):
    t, d = map(int, input().split())
    start = max(t, min(free))
    j = next(i for i in range(k) if free[i] <= start)
    free[j] = start + d
    total_wait += start - t
    out.append(f"{j + 1} {start + d}")
out.append(f"{total_wait / n:.2f}")
print("\n".join(out))

title: Rotate Matrix Rings by K
description:
An R x C matrix is made of concentric rectangular rings (the outer border is ring 1, the border of what remains is ring 2, and so on). Rotate every ring clockwise by K positions: each element moves K steps along its ring in the clockwise direction. A ring that is a single row, a single column, or a single cell is also traversed clockwise (a single cell never changes).

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 40, 0 ≤ K ≤ 109.

Input

The first line contains R C, followed by R lines of C integers, followed by a line containing K.

Output

Print the rotated matrix as R lines of C space-separated integers.

Example: rotating [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]] by 1 gives [[4,1,2],[7,5,3],[8,9,6]].

title: Sudoku Validity Check
description:
Check whether a partially filled 9x9 Sudoku grid is valid: no digit 1-9 may appear more than once in any row, any column, or any of the nine 3x3 boxes. Empty cells are written as 0 and are ignored. (The grid need not be solvable — only check these rules.)

Input

Nine lines, each with nine space-separated integers from 0 to 9.

Output

Print Valid or Invalid.

title: Maximal Rectangle of 1s
description:
Given a binary grid, find the largest axis-aligned rectangle (not necessarily square) containing only 1s and print its area. If there is no 1, print 0.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 120. Brute force over all rectangles is far too slow; treat each row as the base of a histogram and use a monotonic stack (O(R·C)).

Input

The first line contains R C. The next R lines each contain a string of exactly C characters, each 0 or 1.

Output

Print a single integer: the maximum area.
solution:
r, c = map(int, input().split())
g = [input().strip() for _ in range(r)]
h = [0] * c
best = 0
for i in range(r):
    for j in range(c):
        h[j] = h[j] + 1 if g[i][j] == "1" else 0
    st = []
    for j in range(c + 1):
        cur = h[j] if j < c else 0
        while st and h[st[-1]] >= cur:
            top = st.pop()
            width = j - st[-1] - 1 if st else j
            area = h[top] * width
            if area > best:
                best = area
        st.append(j)
print(best)

title: Count Submatrices with Target Sum
description:
Count the number of non-empty rectangular submatrices whose elements sum to exactly T. Two submatrices are different if their corner coordinates differ.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 60, |a[i][j]| ≤ 5, |T| ≤ 104. Checking all O(R²C²) rectangles is too slow; fix a pair of rows and count subarray sums with a hash map (O(R²C)).

Input

The first line contains R C, followed by R lines of C integers, followed by a line containing T.

Output

Print the number of submatrices with sum T.

title: Game of Life on a Torus After K Generations
description:
Run Conway's Game of Life on an R x C torus: the grid wraps around, so the left edge neighbours the right edge and the top neighbours the bottom . The 8 neighbours of cell (i, j) are ((i+di) mod R, (j+dj) mod C) for all di, dj in {-1, 0, 1} except (0, 0); on very small grids the same cell may be counted several times (even the cell itself). Rules: a live cell with 2 or 3 live neighbours survives; a dead cell with exactly 3 live neighbours is born; every other cell is dead in the next generation.

Print the grid after K generations. K can be as large as 1018, so you cannot simulate every step: the board's state must eventually repeat — detect the cycle and skip ahead. For all test data the state repeats within the first 3000 generations.

Constraints: 1 ≤ R, C ≤ 10, 0 ≤ K ≤ 1018.

Input

The first line contains R C K. The next R lines each contain a string of C characters, 1 (alive) or 0 (dead).

Output

Print the grid after K generations as R strings of 0/1.

title: K-th Smallest in a Multiplication Table
description:
The M x N multiplication table is the matrix with table[i][j] = i · j for 1 ≤ i ≤ M, 1 ≤ j ≤ N. Its rows and columns are sorted. Find the K-th smallest value among all M·N entries (counting duplicates).

Constraints: 1 ≤ M, N ≤ 2·104, 1 ≤ K ≤ M·N. The table can have 4·108 entries, so do not build it: binary search on the answer x, counting how many entries are ≤ x row by row.

Input

One line with three integers M N K.

Output

Print the K-th smallest entry.
